text:
alex: seeing sustained GPU pool exhaustion in eu-west-1a; autoscaler keeps adding nodes then immediately hitting ENI/eni-attach errors and pods get evicted. charts show 100% GPU util in nodepool-gpu-batch and a spike of pending pods.

oncall-bot: alert: GPU_POOL_UTILIZATION_HIGH for nodepool-gpu-batch (eu-west-1a) — 12 warnings in 5m.

mira: ack. are these spot or on-demand nodes?

raj: spot-heavy. cloud API shows capacity shortage for p4xlarge in eu-west-1a, lots of reclaimed instances. fallback to on-demand not configured for this nodegroup.

alex: logs from cluster-autoscaler: `scale up failed: failed to attach ENI: request limit exceeded` repeatedly. autoscaler then marks probes unhealthy and removes nodes -> pod churn.

infra-bot: action: attempted autoscaler-probe-retry 3/3; suggestion: add fallback nodegroup with on-demand and higher priorityClass, or temporarily increase ENI quota via cloud console.

mira: priority: immediate mitigation. plan: 1) cordon+drain a subset of old spot nodes to stop thrash, 2) create a small on-demand nodegroup with `node.kubernetes.io/preemptible: "false"` and `node.kubernetes.io/fallback: "true"`, 3) patch scheduler to prefer the on-demand via `priorityClass` for critical batch jobs.

alex: will run `kubectl cordon <node>` and `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` on 3 nodes in eu-west-1a now.

raj: creating on-demand pool now with `eksctl create nodegroup --cluster=infra-prod --name=gpu-fallback-euw1a --instance-type=p4d.24xlarge --nodes=2 --nodes-min=1 --nodes-max=4 --labels=type=fallback` (cloud provisioning in progress).

Sophia: quick note — some researcher jobs set `tolerations: [{key: "dedicated", operator: "Exists", effect: "NoSchedule"}]` and no resource requests. They bypass scheduling controls. We should reject pods without GPU requests at admission.

mira: good call. emergency admission patch: add mutating webhook to enforce `resources.limits.nvidia.com/gpu > 0` for pods that are allowed in gpu nodepools. I'll open a short-lived policy.

alex: drain done on nodes ng-spot-12, ng-spot-15, ng-spot-18. pod eviction rate dropped.

infra-bot: cloud: new nodegroup gpu-fallback-euw1a entered Ready state (2 nodes). kube: nodes registered with labels `type=fallback`.

raj: scaled up fallback and patched critical cronjobs to `priorityClassName: system-cluster-critical` -> pods started scheduling onto fallback nodes. GPU pending count dropped from 68 -> 9 in ~6m.

alex: running `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,NODE:.spec.nodeName,REQ:.spec.containers[*].resources.requests` -> shows most pending were under-requesting. snippet: `research-sweep-97   <none>   []` 

sophia: I'll follow up to add admission rule and small docs for research team about setting gpu requests + priority.

mira: longer term: add autoscaler policy: fallback nodegroup with weight and preferred for critical workloads, and a throttle window to prevent immediate scale down when ENI errors spike. Also request quota increase for ENIs in eu-west-1a from cloud.

alex: mitigation closed for now, monitoring. leaving 1 fallback node to absorb churn. I'll post a short incident writeup after tidy. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: incident note: mitigation applied 1725001320 — reduced pending GPU pods, fallback nodes created. continue monitoring for 1h.

mira: thanks team. follow-ups: PR for admission webhook, autoscaler policy change, and quota ticket. assigning to @sophia, @raj, @alex respectively.
